transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Monroe (Aether Eng Manager), Jordan Lee (Aether CTO), Maya Rivera (Aether DevOps)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Redwood PLG/self-serve API quickstart, free credits and time-to-first-token. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated/private for an internal assistant and embeddings-based search. High-level security requirements (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS) discussed. Agreed next steps: send pricing, spin up trial project, run baseline perf tests with customer payloads.

Topics:
- Quickstart and time-to-first-token
- Free/trial credits and quotas
- Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Security and compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, data retention)
- Latency/cost expectations and benchmark plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 40 minutes, quick intros?
[00:06] Alex (Aether): Hey Alex, engineering manager at Aether, I run the ML infra team.
[00:09] Jordan (Aether): Jordan here, CTO, curious about infra and cost.
[00:12] Maya (Aether): Maya - DevOps, will own any VPC/on-prem setup.
[00:15] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya, I'm the solutions engineer, I can dig into perf and security details.
[00:18] Samira: Great, high level we wanted to understand your use cases then show how quickstart works and what time-to-first-token looks like. Alex, can you give a bit of context?
[00:28] Alex: Sure, we build an internal assistant for product and support, also want embeddings for semantic search over docs. Right now we prototype with open-source LLMs self-hosted but costs and ops overhead are high. We want a fast path to production and to evaluate hosted first, maybe dedicated or private if we need isolation.
[00:44] Jordan: Our main concerns are cost predictability, latency for chat flows, and data residency — some customer data may require stricter controls.
[00:51] Priya: totally. For hosted we provide the Redwood API, quick to sign up, free credits to get started, and a console. Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput. Private is the VPC/on-prem route for regulated workloads.
[01:05] Alex: How long until we can send our first token? like, literally time-to-first-token.
[01:10] Samira: Good question. With the PLG quickstart you sign up, create an API key in the console and you can call the REST API with a cURL command in under 10 minutes; we've seen teams get to first token in 5-15 minutes. We'll share a step-by-step quickstart link.
[01:22] Maya: Are there SDKs or do we have to do raw HTTP?
[01:25] Priya: Both. We have official SDKs for Python, Node, and a cURL snippet in the console. Streaming responses and function-calling are supported.
[01:32] Jordan: What about rate limits on the trial? If we spin up for testing, what are free credits and quotas?
[01:38] Samira: For PLG quickstart new accounts get $500 in free credits for 30 days in the trial tier, subject to fair use. Rate limits are soft initially but we can bump them for POC. I'll include the exact numbers in the follow-up.
[01:51] Alex: Nice. Regarding models, do you host multiple variants? We care about cheap, fast embeddings and low-latency chat.
[01:58] Priya: Our model catalog has optimized open models with performance profiles. For embeddings we have smaller fast models; for chat we have low-latency variants and quantized options. The console shows per-token latency and cost breakdown.
[02:10] Maya: Security — we need SOC2, SSO, KMS integration and audit logs. Also data retention policy.
[02:18] Priya: We are SOC2 compliant, support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations for Private deployments. For hosted we provide customer-configurable retention windows and audit logs; for Dedicated/Private you get more control and can use customer-managed KMS. I'll attach our security pack.
[02:34] Jordan: If we start hosted and later move to Dedicated, will the API surface change?
[02:39] Samira: No — one of our differentiators is a consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private. You can pin model versions and rollout policies; switching deployment modes is designed to be minimal friction.
[02:52] Alex: Latency — our P95 target is 250ms for short chat turns, higher for longer context. Can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[02:59] Priya: That depends on model and sequence lengths. For shorter prompts the low-latency variants on hosted often hit 150-300ms P95 in our benchmarks. For stricter SLOs you can use Dedicated with reserved GPU pools and autoscaling. We'll run a baseline with your payloads to confirm.
[03:16] Alex: Sounds good. About embeddings and cost: do you charge per token or per embedding?
[03:21] Samira: Embeddings are per-embedding unit, chat/generation is per-token. The console breaks down token costs and we have Optimize suggestions for batching and caching to lower unit costs.
[03:33] Maya: For Private, what's the on-prem packaging like? We are air-gapped for some clients.
[03:38] Priya: Private supports on-prem deployments with a customer-managed control plane option; air-gapped installs are possible for enterprise agreements. It involves a separate licensing and support contract.
[03:48] Jordan: If we do a POC we want to run a few hundred QPS synthetic load and also a long-context scenario, e.g., 8k tokens. How does Redwood handle KV cache and batching?
[03:58] Priya: Our serving runtime supports KV cache management and continuous batching; the kernel selection optimizes for sequence length. For long-context we have memory-optimized paths and quantization-friendly execution. For your 8k scenario we'll recommend model variants and quantization.
[04:14] Alex: Ok, operationally, who will own infra for a hosted trial? We want to integrate with our CI to run smoke tests.
[04:19] Samira: For hosted, Redwood owns the infrastructure. You get API keys, can set up test projects, and run CI calls against the API. For Dedicated/Private, you'll coordinate with our solutions team on capacity and network setup.
[04:33] Maya: Are there VPC peering options for Dedicated?
[04:36] Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink in cloud regions; Private supports customer-managed networking. We'll document the network patterns and firewall rules.
[04:46] Jordan: Data residency — can we restrict model serving to EU regions?
[04:50] Priya: Yes, you can route requests by region and pin your deployment to specific regions; for Private you control the environment directly.
[04:56] Alex: Any gotchas around throttling or tokenization differences across models?
[04:59] Priya: Tokenization varies by model family, and the console shows token counts for requests. Throttling can be tuned for Dedicated. For hosted, fair-use limits apply but we can raise requests for POCs.
[05:12] Samira: Quick demo idea: we'll send the quickstart link and a cURL snippet so you can hit the API immediately. Priya can provision a trial project and run a small benchmark.
[05:20] Alex: That would be ideal. Also can you share an example of streaming? We want to avoid large tail latency on interactive flows.
[05:27] Priya: Streaming is supported; we stream token deltas and have server-side heuristics to reduce tail latency. We'll include a sample SDK stream snippet.
[05:36] Maya: On the security docs — will you share SOC2 reports and a data processing addendum?
[05:40] Samira: Yes will attach SOC2 and DPA in the follow-up.
[05:44] Jordan: Pricing — we need a ballpark to justify a POC internally.
[05:48] Samira: I'll share tiered pricing in the follow-up; the trial credits should cover most of your POC. After that we have usage-based pricing for hosted and reserved/committed pricing for Dedicated.
[05:58] Alex: If we wanted a Dedicated pilot, what lead time do you typically see?
[06:02] Priya: For Reserved Dedicated pools it's usually a few weeks to provision, depending on region and capacity. Private on-prem takes longer because of networking and compliance. For quick validation use hosted trial.
[06:15] Maya: One operational detail: our CI will rotate API keys automatically, any tips?
[06:20] Priya: We support API key rotation; you can create service keys and rotate them from the console and update CI. We'll add best-practices in the notes.
[06:29] Alex: Great. Any reference benchmarks you can share?
[06:32] Priya: We'll share our Redwood perf sheet showing P95/P99 across models and sequence lengths. It will be in the follow-up along with quickstart steps.
[06:41] Jordan: On compliance, for Dedicated do you enable customer-managed KMS?
[06:44] Priya: Yes for Dedicated/Private you can use customer-managed KMS/HSM. For hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit; we do not have customer KMS for the standard hosted plan, but enterprise options exist.
[06:58] Alex: Ok lets recap next steps please.
[07:02] Samira: Recap — I will send pricing + free credits details, SOC2/DPA, quickstart link and cURL+SDK snippets. Priya will provision a trial project and run baseline latency tests; Alex will share sample payloads and traffic patterns. We'll schedule a perf benchmark session next week.
[07:18] Jordan: Sounds good.
[07:20] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[07:22] Samira: Thanks all. We'll follow up in the next 48 hours with the docs and provisioning.

Notes and imperfections: occasional transcript errors present, some speaker overlaps and filler words. References: quickstart link (console.redwood.ai/quickstart), security pack doc (redwood.ai/security-pack.pdf), perf spreadsheet (redwood.ai/perf-benchmarks.xlsx) — we will send links in follow-up.

End of transcript.
